![What Causes Sudden Hair Shedding? | Goodman Dermatology](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/10180446-2787-0139-0000-787fbf353dde:4)
Shedding is `the natural or medical process of losing an outer covering—such as hair, skin, fur, or feathers—or releasing particles like viruses or fluid`.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shedding)[[2]](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/shedding)

### Human Hair Shedding

- **Normal Rate:** Losing about **50 to 100 hairs a day** is a healthy part of the growth cycle.
- **Telogen Effluvium:** Temporary excessive shedding can happen **2 to 3 months** after a physical or emotional stressor, such as high fever, surgery, childbirth, or rapid weight loss.
- **Identification:** Hairs that shed naturally have a small white bulb at the root, unlike broken strands.
- **Management:** Use a wide-tooth comb, avoid tight hairstyles or heavy heat styling, and maintain good scalp care and nutrition.[[1]](https://store.mayoclinic.com/education/hair-thinning-vs-hair-shedding-products/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G0gPxg94AuM&vl=en&t=31)[[3]](https://www.goodmandermatology.com/blog/what-causes-sudden-hair-shedding/)[[4]](https://bosleymd.com/blogs/hair-thinning/hair-shedding-vs-hair-loss-key-differences)[[5]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OEjQcYlOCok&t=8)

### Pet Shedding

- **Seasonal Changes:** Dogs and cats naturally "blow" or lose their undercoats in the **spring and fall** as temperatures shift.
- **Management:** Regular brushing with a proper undercoat rake or shedding tool removes dead hair before it spreads around the home.
- **Red Flags:** See a veterinarian if shedding comes with bald patches, red or inflamed skin, or constant itching.[[1]](https://www.webmd.com/pets/dogs/excessive-shedding-dogs)[[2]](https://www.aaha.org/resources/pets-and-shedding/)

### Other Types of Shedding

- **Skin Desquamation:** The body constantly sheds dead skin cells from its outer layer.
- **Moulting / Ecdysis:** Reptiles, amphibians, and insects shed old skin or outgrown exoskeletons to grow.
- **Viral Shedding:** A medical term for when a host body releases virus particles into the environment.[[1]](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/shedding)[[2]](https://www.vocabulary.com/dictionary/shedding)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moulting)
